conflicts.fact: Where the wilting plants are located on the farmer's field, and what the farmer reports she saw
conflicts.versions: Lesson 1: border plants are yellow and drooping while interior plants are green; the farmer never saw any insect. Lesson 5: she walks along the edge early in the morning and sees NO insect, NO fungus, NO visible damage above the soil. Both agree on the edge, but Lesson 5 adds the dry season and says soil pests are most active then, which Lesson 1 does not state.

conflicts.fact: When the cumulative/inference model was started and what it contains
conflicts.versions: Lesson 1: learners draw a first baseline model (evidence → conclusion diagram) on Day 1. Lesson 2: learners start a new mind-map 'Model Version 1 — Lesson 2' with General Science at the centre. Lesson 3: expands 'the personal inference model they began building in Lesson 2' as HIDDEN CAUSE → INDIRECT EVIDENCE → INFERENCE → CONCLUSION, which conflicts with the Lesson 2 mind-map. Lesson 6: 'Inference Model' built 'since Lesson 3'. Lesson 8: final model compared with the 'Lesson 1 sketch model'.

conflicts.fact: Wording of the Driving Question and the DQB structure
conflicts.versions: Lesson 1: DQB has three columns ('Questions about the Phenomenon/General Science/Careers & Kenya') and the closing hook is 'If the farmer never saw the pest, how could she possibly know it was there?'. Lesson 2: column 'Questions we now have' with themes. Lesson 3 cites a 'DQB protocol established in Lesson 1' of green and orange sticky notes, which Lesson 1 never set up (it used three columns). Lessons 3–8 give the driving question as 'How does a scientist know something is true when they cannot see it directly…'.
Lessons 1–4 and 6 leave the farmer unnamed; Lesson 5 names her Akinyi and Lesson 7 'Mama Akinyi'. Lesson 5 also adds the dry season as evidence, which Lesson 1 lists only as 'time of season'.

conflicts.fact: Duration of the Lesson 1 model-building task
conflicts.versions: Lesson 1 learner text says 'final 5 minutes', while the teacher says 'last five minutes' and then gives 'exactly 4 minutes'.

conflicts.fact: Number of Lessons used for DQB sorting and the colour coding
conflicts.versions: Lesson 7 sorts DQB cards into three columns (Answer/Partly/Don't Know) and uses green/yellow/red dots, and says yellow questions will be revisited in 'Lesson 8'. Lesson 8 says the board is 'colour-coded for the first time' with green ticks, yellow arrows and red question marks, contradicting Lesson 7's earlier colour coding.

conflicts.fact: Which sub-strand the unresolved questions lead to
conflicts.versions: Lesson 7 maps the pest-underground question to Sub-Strand 1.4 Transport in Plants and 1.6 Plant Growth, with future sub-strands The Cell, Nutrition, Respiration. Lesson 8 bridges root destruction questions to Sub-Strand 1.2 The Cell.

conflicts.fact: Lesson 7 length and lesson count claims
conflicts.versions: Lesson 7 is called an '80-minute' session, while the other lessons' activities are timed for standard-length lessons; Lesson 2 says the model grows 'across all eight lessons'.
